t: The “September Surge” is here - yes, even in India 👀 The term comes from the US, where...
d: The “September Surge” is here - yes, even in India 👀 The term comes from the US, where hiring restarts after summer and companies begin filling roles before the year-end slowdown. But why does that matter here? Many US companies now have large engineering, product, AI and operations teams in India. So when global hiring opens up, some of that headcount can translate into India opportunities, especially across MNCs, GCCs and global tech companies. Add India’s own end-of-Q2 and festive hiring push, and “September Surge” becomes real in India too. SAVE this and do these five things ASAP: 1️⃣ Apply early Create profiles on @wellfoundhq , @cutshorthq , @instahyre , @naukridotcom , YC Work at a Startup, @himalayasapp and @remoteok Apply within 24 to 48 hours of a role being posted. Older listings are more crowded or may already be closing internally. 2️⃣ Fix your LinkedIn Use a professional photo and role-specific headline. Add your experience properly and feature your resume, portfolio or best project. Use this structure while writing: Action → Context → Result → Stakeholders Recruiters should understand you within 6 seconds. 3️⃣ Reach out Contact the hiring manager, recruiter, founder or relevant employees who could refer you or directly cold email asking for job. Keep your message short: • Who you are • Why the role interests you • Why you are relevant • Where they can see your work - Proof 4️⃣ Build proof using AI Use ChatGPT or Claude to create a relevant project, case study, prototype or workflow for your target role. One strong proof-of-work project can help you stand out more than another generic certificate. 5️⃣ Track everything Create a sheet with the company, role, date applied, person contacted, follow-up date and status. For the next 30 days: Apply early. Reach out consistently. Ask for referrals. Build proof. Follow up properly. Follow @geekyballer.ai to WIN in the AI era. Strengthen foundational skills • Top academic systems emphasize fundamentals: • Master mental math and logic • Strengthen reading comprehension • Build strong writing habits • Deepen conceptual understanding before memorizing Strong foundations make advanced work easier. 3. Use active learning, not passive learning To reach high competence: • Teach what you learned to someone else • Do practice problems instead of rereading • Summarize concepts in your own words • Quiz yourself regularly • Active recall → long-term mastery. 4. Cultivate discipline, not obsession Some students in high-pressure systems face stress, exhaustion, and burnout. You don’t want that. Healthy discipline: • Sleep at least 7–8 hours • Take one full rest day each week • Exercise regularly • Keep hobbies Your brain works best when your body is supported. 5. Study deeply, not just widely To reach “overeducated” levels in a positive sense: • Choose 1–2 subjects to become exceptional in • Read academic books, papers, or advanced materials • Work on long-term projects or research • Enter competitions, labs, or academic circles • Depth creates expertise. 6. t: CORTISOL IS THE ENEMY OF A SHARP FACE AND FAT LOSS
d: CORTISOL IS THE #1 ENEMY OF A SHARP FACE AND FAT LOSS. HERE ARE 5 WAYS TO GET YOUR CONTOURS BACK: 1. MAGNESIUM FROM FOOD (pumpkin seeds, spinach, 85%+ dark chocolate) Helps lower cortisol over a few weeks. Magnesium calms your nervous system and dials down your stress-hormone response. A handful of raw seeds a day or spinach with dinner — and that morning puffiness starts to fade. 2. SLEEP IN TOTAL DARKNESS, LIGHTS OUT BY 11 PM Between 11 PM and 2 AM your body produces the most melatonin, which keeps cortisol in check. Even a dim glow from a charger can bump up nighttime cortisol. Kill the LEDs, hang blackout curtains. Give it a week — your face looks fresher. 3. CUT SUGAR AND ALCOHOL AT NIGHT Sugar spikes insulin and drives inflammation, which feeds cortisol. Alcohol drops cortisol at first, then rebounds it hours later (that’s the next-morning puff after a glass of wine). Swap the late dessert for a handful of nuts, and the wine for chamomile tea. 4. WARM WATER WITH A PINCH OF SALT + LEMON IN THE MORNING Cortisol often runs high when sodium and potassium are out of balance. Salt gives you sodium, lemon gives you potassium. This helps calm your morning cortisol surge and flush extra water out of your tissues. Sip it slowly, 20 minutes before you eat. 5. A MORNING WALK WITH NO PHONE (15–20 MIN) Morning light + movement reset your circadian rhythm, and no screens give your brain a real break. People who walk in the morning without their phone tend to carry lower cortisol all day — and a less puffy face. RECAP: → MAGNESIUM FROM FOOD → DARK ROOM, LIGHTS OUT BY 11 → NO SUGAR OR ALCOHOL AT NIGHT → WARM SALT + LEMON WATER IN THE AM → PHONE-FREE MORNING WALK Puffiness drops. Your face gets sharper. Fat loss moves faster. I’m building a simple 7-Day Face De-Puff Reset. Comment “RESET” if you want early access — I’ll DM the first version. Follow for more: @alen_troyan.

t: These 7 work habits actually helped me get promoted 👨🏻‍💻📈 They weren’t loud
d: These 7 work habits actually helped me get promoted 👨🏻‍💻📈 They weren’t loud. They weren’t fancy. But they worked. For a long time, I thought working hard = career growth. But I eventually realized something important: Doing good work isn’t enough. You also need to make your work visible. These are the habits I started building: 1. Track your weekly wins 📝 Every Friday, write down 3 things you achieved that week — even the small ones. It helps you recognize your progress and makes performance reviews much easier. 2. Keep your manager updated. You don’t need to brag about your work. Just share what you worked on, the impact you created, and what you learned. Visibility matters in corporate life. 3. Ask for growth-focused feedback. Instead of asking, “How am I doing?” Ask: “What do I need to improve to be ready for the next level?” That question can completely change the conversation around your career. 4. Speak up in meetings. 🗣️ You don’t need to talk the most. Even one useful point, question, or idea can show initiative and build your professional presence. 5. Take ownership, not just tasks. Don’t just complete what’s assigned to you. Understand the problem, suggest solutions, and follow through. Be the person people can rely on. 6. Document what you learn. Solutions, processes, mistakes, learnings — keep a record. It saves time, makes you better at your job, and shows that you’re constantly improving. 7. Learn beyond your current role. 🚀 Don’t only learn what you need for today’s task. Keep building skills that prepare you for the next role, next project, and next level. These habits didn’t change my career overnight. But over time, they changed how I worked, how I communicated, and how people perceived my contribution. And that made a difference. Save this. Start with one habit this week. Your career growth doesn’t always need a big move. Sometimes, it starts with small habits done consistently. 👨🏻‍💻 #corporatelife #itprofessionals #office #career #growth.

d: Everyone is talking about GPT‑6 Astra’s 99.9% score, but here is the precise context. ARC Prize ran and published both evaluations. Astra scored 62.7% with the Standard harness at max reasoning, costing $26,098. It scored 99.9% with the Provider Adapter at high reasoning, costing $18,817. The Adapter preserves reasoning between calls, so the difference came from how context was carried forward, not who ran the test. Claude Opus 5 scored 30.2% at high reasoning with the Standard harness. Therefore, 62.7% versus 30.2% uses the same harness, but different reasoning settings. More importantly, ARC‑AGI‑3 tests whether AI can explore a completely new game, learn its rules and complete the goal. It doesn’t prove AGI is here, but it shows how quickly AI is improving. Don’t wait for AGI. Start using AI for one repeated task today. . . . t: 🎬- Sapta Sagaradaache Ello (2023, Kannada), directed by Hemanth M
d: 🎬- Sapta Sagaradaache Ello (2023, Kannada), directed by Hemanth M. Rao, unfolds like a quiet ache that slowly deepens with time. At its core, it follows Manu, played with striking vulnerability by Rakshit Shetty, a simple man whose life revolves around love, loyalty, and doing the right thing—until one decision changes everything. Opposite him, Rukmini Vasanth brings a soft yet emotionally grounded presence, making their relationship feel lived-in rather than cinematic. The film doesn’t rush its story; it lets moments breathe, allowing you to sit with its characters and the weight of their choices. What makes the film linger isn’t just the narrative, but the way it captures longing, distance, and the quiet sacrifices people make for love. There’s an unspoken tension in its silences—the kind where words aren’t needed because the pain is already understood. The atmosphere feels almost tactile: dimly lit rooms, passing time, and a sense of something slipping away just when it felt within reach. It’s less about dramatic twists and more about emotional erosion—how love endures, but also how it changes under pressure. By the end, it doesn’t try to give you closure; it leaves you with a feeling, one that stays long after the film is over..

t: DAY 11/100 — STOP MEMORIZING CODE Here’s a small test
d: DAY 11/100 — STOP MEMORIZING CODE Here’s a small test. Look at the code in the video Don’t run it. Don’t use AI. Just tell me… what will it print? If you got it wrong, that’s actually good. Because this is a skill I want you to build. When you see code, don’t immediately think, ‘What does this line mean?’ Start asking: ‘What is going to happen next?’ That’s how programmers think. For example, if I have a loop… don’t just memorize how a for loop looks. Predict: How many times will it run? What will the variable contain after each iteration? What will happen when the condition becomes false? Then run the code and check your prediction. If you’re wrong, don’t feel bad. Your brain just found something it didn’t understand. And that’s exactly what learning looks like. From today… don’t just read code. Predict it #programming #coding #engineering #btech #career.

Kalakalappu (2012) — transl. Humour — is a Tamil comedy film written and directed by Sundar C, produced by his wife Khushbu under Avni Cinemax and UTV Motion Pictures, a Tamil adaptation of the German comedy "Soul Kitchen". Starring Vimal as Kannan and Shiva as Raghu, alongside Anjali and Oviya as the female leads, with Santhanam in a scene-stealing comic role. Music by Vijay Ebenezer, cinematography by U. K. Senthil Kumar, editing by Praveen K. L. and N. B. Srikanth. Released 11 May 2012 — runtime 154 minutes. Originally titled "Masala Café" before being renamed. Raghu, a struggling restaurant owner, is fighting to keep his family-owned eatery from shutting down under debt — only for a health inspector determined to shut the place down to walk into his life, complicating things further, while his brother's arrival throws the chaos into overdrive. A pure, feel-good multi-starrer comedy built on sharp writing, perfectly timed slapstick and effortless chemistry between its four leads — widely regarded as one of Sundar C's finest comic outings, with fans still calling it superior to its 2018 sequel. Became a commercial success and was later remade in Telugu as "Jump Jilani". t: Suppose your credit card limit is ₹1,00,000 and your statement/due details are:
d: Suppose your credit card limit is ₹1,00,000 and your statement/due details are: | * Bill generated: 5th July | * Payment due date: 25th July | * Current outstanding: ₹60,000 | ₹60,000 ÷ ₹1,00,000 = 60% utilisation ⚠️ | Here is how the strategy is actually done: | 1. Don’t blindly wait for the due date. Around 10th July, open your credit card app and check the total outstanding/current outstanding. | 2. Make an early part-payment. Suppose you pay ₹40,000. Your outstanding reduces from ₹60,000 to roughly ₹20,000, bringing utilisation to about 20%. CIBIL educational guidance describes around 30% utilisation as a healthy benchmark and warns against over-leveraging the available limit. | 3. Continue using the card carefully. t: “Tell me about yourself” is NOT an invitation to recite your resume
d: “Tell me about yourself” is NOT an invitation to recite your resume. Your interviewer already has your resume in front of them. ❌ “Myself Batool, I’ve been working here at ABC for 2 years, my total experience is 6 years…” Instead, think of your introduction like a short career story. Here’s the structure I’d recommend: 1️⃣ Greeting ✅ “My name’s Batool, thank you for having me.” Simple. Polite. No need to overcomplicate it. 2️⃣ Background ✅ “I come from Bangalore; I hold a management degree with a specialisation in HR.” Give them a little context about who you are. 3️⃣ Backstory ✅ “This field was never something I originally intended to get into…” This is where you make it human. A short, interesting backstory can make your introduction far more memorable than simply listing your qualifications. 4️⃣ Current Role ✅ “I’m currently an HR Generalist handling the end-to-end employee lifecycle…” Now bring the conversation to what you actually do today. 📌 Use keywords that are relevant to the job description: If the role requires employee lifecycle management, HRIS, workforce analytics or stakeholder management, and you genuinely have that experience, make sure you mention it. 5️⃣ Relevant Skills / Tech Stack ✅ “I work with tools like SAP SuccessFactors, Darwinbox and Power BI…” Don’t randomly list every tool you’ve ever touched. Highlight the ones that actually matter for the role you’re interviewing for. 6️⃣ Measurable Impact ✅ “I redesigned our onboarding process, which brought early attrition down by around 18%…” This is where you move from “this is what I do” to “this is what I’ve actually achieved.” ✅✅ The simple formula: Greeting → Background → Backstory → Current Role → Relevant Skills → Measurable Impact And one important thing: don’t memorise this word-for-word. You want to sound prepared, not rehearsed. Your goal isn’t to tell them everything you’ve ever done. It’s to give them enough context to think: “Okay, this person makes sense for this role. Tell me more.” That’s exactly where you want your introduction.

d: 🚩The new way companies are messing with your notice period ————————- Recruiters are asking candidates (especially those with 60-90 day notice periods) to onboard as a “consultant” with the new company BEFORE their LWD at the current one. That means your start date may get marked while you’re still employed elsewhere, creating an employment overlap that follows you for the rest of your career. t: Premam (2015) stands as a landmark triumph in contemporary Malayalam cinema, a film that...
d: Premam (2015) stands as a landmark triumph in contemporary Malayalam cinema, a film that seamlessly transforms the familiar trope of coming-of-age romance into an enduring cultural phenomenon. Directed, written, and edited with sharp artistic precision by Alphonse Puthren, the narrative beautifully chronicles fourteen years in the life of George David, tracing his emotional evolution across three distinct chapters of love, heartbreak, and eventual maturity. From the clumsy, sun-drenched innocence of a high-school crush to the passionate, high-stakes romance of his rowdy college days, and finally to the quiet, bittersweet acceptance of adult companionship, the film serves as a universal mirror for the audience's own nostalgic journeys. Most notably by introducing Sai Pallavi's character, Malar, whose makeup-free appearance revolutionized beauty standards for leading women in South Indian cinema. Combined with its brilliant situational humor and a deeply relatable exploration of grief and healing, Premam transcends the boundaries of a simple romantic comedy, remaining a masterclass in how cinema can capture the raw, fleeting essence of human affection..

t: ❗5 things you’re saying wrong on your offer call
d: ❗5 things you’re saying wrong on your offer call. ———————— ❌ Giving a fixed number ✅ Giving a range: when you say one number, you’ve capped yourself, there’s no room to negotiate down to. A range gives HR space to work within, and you’ll almost always land closer to the top than if you’d just said 12. ❌ Leaving value on the table ✅ Leveraging your availability: companies pay a premium for speed, especially when they’re trying to close a role fast. If you can join sooner than notice period allows, that’s leverage...don’t give it away for free. ❌ Accepting blindly ✅ Asking for clarity first: CTC is not take-home. A high number with a shady fixed-to-variable split can mean you’re earning way less than it looks like on paper. Always know what you’re actually signing up for before you say yes. ❌ Doing the company a favor for free ✅ Negotiating the buyout: encashing your leaves and rushing out helps the company, not you. If they want you early, that urgency is worth something, ask them to pay for it. ❌ Settling for less ✅ Asking for a bonus instead: “No budget for a hike” doesn’t mean the conversation is over. A one-time joining bonus doesn’t touch their fixed-cost budget the way a CTC bump does, so it’s often an easier yes for them. ———————— FOLLOW @batooloncareer 👉 Resume Review 👉 Interview Prep 👉 Salary Negotiation 👉 Promotions 👉 Exit Strategy.

t: He says that he “steals from real life” and that the idea for the film began with...
d: He says that he “steals from real life” and that the idea for the film began with something he personally witnessed. While returning home after watching a movie, he accompanied a friend who was dropping his girlfriend home. On MG Road, a police officer was conducting a drunk-driving check. A car stopped, and when the officer went to check it, the car suddenly sped away. The car did not directly hit the officer, but he lost his balance and fell. His head hit the pavement. Hemanth and his friends stopped, picked him up and put him in an auto. The officer died in front of him. They then went to the police station and dealt with what followed. At that time, Hemanth says he had no intention of making a film about the incident. He was simply writing. A few days later, he learned that the person who was actually driving the car was not the person who admitted to the incident; somebody else took responsibility and went to jail. That incident stayed with Hemanth and made him wonder about the person’s life beyond the incident — what if he had a girlfriend? What if they had dreams? What kind of life did he have? Those questions became the starting point for the film. He says this happened around ten years before Sapta Sagaradaache Ello. He initially began writing a script based on that incident, but over the years the story evolved, with new characters and ideas emerging. His larger point is that writers should “steal from real life.” Everyone has unique experiences and interesting people around them. Those small observations can become the foundation for believable characters and stories. He explains that you don't need to experience something extreme yourself to write about an emotion. If you've been in love, for example, you already know what love does to your mind and body. You can use your own experiences and observations to understand other people's emotions and lives. 👉 Watch video full video @studenttribe Youtube channel #HemanthRao #saptasagaradaacheello { Hemanth Rao, Sapta Sagaradaache Ello, Kannada Cinema, Indian Cinema, Filmmaking, Storytelling, Cinema, Movies, Director, Film Lover, Movie Lover, Real Life }.

t: Salary negotiation is not just about getting a few extra lakhs in your next paycheck
d: Salary negotiation is not just about getting a few extra lakhs in your next paycheck. It can have a much bigger impact on your overall career earnings. 💰 | Script Link : | Let’s say you receive a ₹12 LPA offer, but after negotiating, the company agrees to ₹14 LPA. | At first, you might think: | “It’s just ₹2 lakhs more.” | But that ₹2 lakhs becomes part of your salary base. | Now imagine you receive a 10% hike every year. That additional amount also gets carried forward into your future salary calculations. Over the next few years, the gap can become significantly larger. | And there’s another important factor — your next job switch. | When you move to another company, your current CTC can become one of the factors considered during compensation discussions. | Having a higher CTC can give you a higher starting point for your next negotiation. | Of course, your next company should ideally evaluate you based on the role, level, skills, experience, and market value, not simply give you a percentage hike on your current salary. | That’s why you shouldn’t negotiate only by saying: | ❌ “I want a 40% hike.” | Instead, understand your market value and communicate your expectation based on: | ✅ Your years of experience | ✅ Your technical skills | ✅ Your achievements | ✅ The responsibilities of the new role | ✅ Current market compensation | ✅ The complete CTC structure | ✅ Other genuine offers, if you have them | And remember, CTC is not the same as take-home salary. | Understand the offer. | Know your market value. | Set your target. | And negotiate. | Because sometimes, one uncomfortable conversation with HR can be worth lakhs over the next few years. | Your salary negotiation today can influence your salary growth tomorrow. 🚀 | Save this post if you’re planning to switch jobs, and share it with someone who is currently negotiating an offer. | #SalaryNegotiation #SalaryNegotiationTips #CareerTips #CareerGrowth #JobSwitch JobOffer CTC SalaryHike SoftwareEngineer SoftwareDeveloper ITJobs TechJobs TechCareer https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dxE2H-DB7_X3vKnKTmMnZtxxI7Qw9dduNA2GZ9pZCFU/edit?usp=sharing

d: So, what should you say instead?👀 If you “actually have an offer”, be transparent about it. You can say: “Yes, 1 currently have an offer from another organization. The offered CTC is? LPA, and the expected joining date is _ However, I’m still exploring opportunities that align better with my career goals!” This gives the recruiter useful information without sounding like you’re using the offer as a threat. If you “don’t have an offer”, simply say: I’m currently exploring a few opportunities, but I don’t have a confirmed offer at the moment. And most importantly: ❌ Don’t create a fake offer. ❌ Don’t inflate the offer amount. ❌ Don’t use a fake offer just to negotiate. An actual offer can strengthen your negotiation. A fake offer can damage your credibility. Recruiter DD’s tip💅 If HR asks about your expected CTC, discuss it based on your experience, skills, current compensation and the responsibilities of the role. You can negotiate without lying. A fake offer might help you in the moment, but it can seriously affect your credibility if the recruiter asks for further details or proof. Be honest. Be strategic. Negotiate professionally💼 Save this before your next HR call📌 #interview #hiring #reels #interviewtips #hr [interview reels, hr, tips, job, hiring, candidate, recruiter, tips, interview, market, salary, offer, office, corporate, outlook, teams, reality].

People think I got lucky. The truth is… I completely changed the way I approached my career. When I was earning ₹10,000/month, I was doing what most people do. ➡️ Go to work. ➡️ Come home. ➡️ Repeat. Then I realized that if nothing changed, neither would my income. This is how I went from ₹10,000/month to ₹1 lakh/month in just one year. 1. I stopped learning just to pass exams. I started learning skills companies actually pay for—Excel, Xero, communication, UK accounting, AI tools, and practical accounting. 2. I invested in myself after my breakup. Instead of feeling sorry for myself, I used that phase to become better. It became the turning point in my career. 3. I switched jobs whenever I stopped learning. I wasn’t chasing job titles—I was chasing skills. Every switch increased my value. 4. I built genuine connections. I connected with recruiters, professionals, and founders on LinkedIn. Your network often creates opportunities before your CV does. 5. I approached clients shamelessly. I sent messages, emails, and connection requests without overthinking. Most ignored me, some rejected me, but a few said yes—and those yeses changed my career. 6. I worked after work. While others relaxed, I kept learning. Those extra hours compounded over time. 7. I improved my communication. Technical skills matter, but if you can’t communicate your value, you’ll always earn less than you’re capable of. 8. I stopped depending on one income source. A job gave me experience and stability, but getting my own clients accelerated my income. 9. I never stopped learning. Every salary increase came after I became more valuable. ⸻ My biggest lesson: ❌ Don’t chase a ₹1 lakh salary. ✅ Chase ₹1 lakh worth of skills. Money is a by-product of the value you create. t: A good-looking resume doesn’t get you shortlisted
d: A good-looking resume doesn’t get you shortlisted. A relevant resume does. Being an HR, one mistake I see every day is candidates applying to every company with the same resume. Please don’t do that. Here’s what I recommend: ✅ Customize your resume for every job. Update it according to the Job Description (JD). ✅ Don’t just list your responsibilities. Highlight your achievements with numbers like revenue, targets, hiring, team size, client portfolio and awards. ✅ Mention your latest experience first with clear responsibilities and measurable results. ✅ If you have a genuine career gap or short job tenure, add a one-line synopsis. It helps recruiters understand your profile better. Just make sure you can confidently explain it during the interview. ✅ Mention only genuine certifications. ✅ Remove unnecessary details like Career Objective, Current CTC, References and Full Address. ✅ Keep your resume clean, relevant and within 1–2 pages. Ask yourself one question before applying: “Would I shortlist this resume in 10 seconds? 📌 Save this post for your next job application. #shorts #viralvideo.

t: My Framework for learning: ⭐️Also comment “Roadmap” and i will share what helped me to...
d: My Framework for learning: ⭐️Also comment “Roadmap” and i will share what helped me to get there MUST Read Every week, I protect just 10 hours. • 2 hours on Friday. • 4 hours on Saturday. • 4 hours on Sunday. Not because I enjoy studying every weekend. Not because I’m motivated all the time. I do it because I know the person I want to become won’t be built during office hours. Now imagine this. 10 hours every week. That’s 520 hours in a year. Five hundred and twenty hours. Just pause and think about that. What could your life look like after 520 focused hours? You could learn a skill that companies are hiring for. Build projects that make recruiters notice you. Earn certifications. Become confident in interviews. Improve your communication. Or finally make that career switch you’ve been talking about for years. And here’s the part people often get wrong. I’m not sacrificing my weekends. A day has 24 hours. I’m investing only 4 focused hours. The other 20 hours are still for my family, friends, workouts, movies, travel, hobbies, or simply doing nothing. I’m not trying to work all day. I’m just refusing to let an entire weekend disappear without investing a little in my future. Because success isn’t built in one massive moment. It’s built in small promises you keep to yourself. Week after week. Month after month. Most people use weekends to escape the life they have. I’m trying to use mine to build the life I want. And maybe that’s the only difference. One year from now, our careers will reflect how we spent our weekends. If you can give Netflix four hours… You can give your future four hours. Your next breakthrough might not need more talent. It might only need one decision. To start this weekend. [ Career, Career Insights, Corporate, Software developer, 9to5].

t: Master’s or Work Experience? 🤔 This is one of the biggest career decisions I had to make...
d: Master’s or Work Experience? 🤔 This is one of the biggest career decisions I had to make after my Bachelor’s. And honestly… I was confused too. I grew up hearing that a Master’s degree would automatically lead to a better career and a better salary. So before making any decision, I spoke to people who had already done their Master’s and to seniors with years of experience in IT. Here’s what I understood from those conversations and my own journey. My biggest learnings: ✅ Don’t do a Master’s just because everyone else is doing it. ✅ Be clear about why you want to pursue it. Is it for: * Better learning? * Domain change? * Management roles? * Studying abroad? * Or only for a higher salary? If it’s only for money… remember that the competition doesn’t end after a Master’s. You still have to stand out. You still have to build skills. You still have to be among the top performers. What I chose After a lot of brainstorming, I decided to continue in the IT industry, focus on my domain, improve my skills, and grow from there. For me, it turned out to be the right decision. That doesn’t mean it’s the right decision for everyone. If you’re confused right now… Ask yourself one question: “What problem am I trying to solve by doing a Master’s?” Once you’re clear about why, the decision becomes much easier. ⚠️ Just to be clear: This reel is completely based on my personal experience, the conversations I had with seniors, and what worked for me. I thought of sharing it because I know many students and early-career professionals are stuck with the same confusion. If this helps even one person make a more informed decision, it’s worth sharing. ❤️ What’s your take? Master’s or work experience? I’d love to hear different perspectives in the comments. 👇 . . . . . . . . . 🔑 keywords: 9to5 life, office, software engineering, corporate life, corporate, pune, salesforce, engineering, switch, career, mindset, weekdays, weekends, office life, 9 to 5, job switch, Masters , experience 📌 Hashtags #viral #corporate #9to5 #career #relatable.

t: The spot where a King’s Minister found God
d: The spot where a King’s Minister found God. 👣🎶 Most people walk the Girivalam path in Thiruvannamalai without realizing they are passing the birthplace of a miracle. This is the Manickavasagar Temple. Here, the great Saint—who gave up his power as a Prime Minister for Annamalaiyar—composed the sacred Thiruvempavai. While standing at this exact location, he was moved by the pure devotion of village girls waking up for their morning prayers. His hymns were so soul-stirring that Annamalaiyar appeared before him in a divine vision right here. ✨ Centuries have passed, but even today, every Margazhi morning in Tamil Nadu still begins with his words. Bhagavan Ramana Maharshi himself confirmed this is the sacred ground where the Saint addressed the mountain. 🏔️ Next time you are in Thiruvannamalai, don’t just walk past. Notice the shape of the temple dome - 𝗽𝘆𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗹, unusual for South Indian temple architecture. The triangle is a pure yantra of the fire element - and the pyramidal roof is its mandala, representing the fire element and the connection to it residing here. 🔱 It is located on the 𝗚𝗶𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗺 path - and according to tradition, going around this temple is equal to performing a full 𝗚𝗶𝗿𝗶𝗽𝗿𝗮𝗱𝗮𝗸𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗮 around the mountain. The Karthikeya deepam is also lit here during 𝗠𝗮𝗵𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝘃𝗮𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗿𝗶 - together with the flame on top of the hill - as it is also the sacred day of the marriage of Shiva and Parvati. 🌋 Don’t come here just to visit and continue walking… Come and 𝘀𝗶𝘁. Be still. Meditate. Om Namah Shivaya 🙏🏻 Follow to discover more hidden sacred spots of Tiruvannamalai 🌿 @living_tiruvannamalai.

t: Most people who visit Tiruvannamalai - go to Girivalam, Darshan, but never explore more…...
d: Most people who visit Tiruvannamalai - go to Girivalam, Darshan, but never explore more… But if you come here for the deeper search… you definitely should explore… And one of the places you should go is the Patala Lingam - inside the Arunachaleswarar Temple. This is one of the most powerful energy spots in Tiruvannamalai - one of those places where meditation happens effortlessly. If you enter through the Eastern Gopuram (Raja Gopuram) and go straight, you will see on the right a small entrance named “Sri Patala Lingam”. You will arrive at the Thousand Pillared Hall and see a staircase leading 15 feet below the temple floor - down to an ancient Lingam… This is the 𝗣𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗮 𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗺. The Lingam itself is ancient - it was the Samadhi of a Jnani, worshipped by saints who lived here long before all the construction above. But the reason we know this place today is because of a 16-year-old boy who arrived in Tiruvannamalai in 1896 with nothing - and found his way down these stairs… 𝗥𝗮𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗮 𝗠𝗮𝗵𝗮𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶 sat for weeks in this dark, damp underground chamber… completely absorbed in Samadhi - without food, without water… while ants and insects devoured his flesh. He felt nothing. He sat here - until devotees found his body covered in wounds and physically carried him out. It was here, in total darkness, below the earth, at the feet of an ancient Lingam - that he attained Cosmic Consciousness… At that time the place was in complete ruin - dark, abandoned, full of snakes and scorpions. It was only because of Ramana - because devotees followed him here - that this shrine was eventually restored to what you see today. Om Namah Shivaya 🙏🏻 Follow to discover more secrets of Tiruvannamalai 🫶🏻 📍 Patala Lingam - Arulmigu Arunachaleswarar Temple, Tiruvannamalai​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​.

1. Kill the illusion of “someday.” Someday I’ll start the business. Someday I’ll take the trip. Someday never comes. Start now, even if it’s messy. 2. Take your parents to lunch. I lost my dad out of nowhere at 26. I’d give anything for one more meal, one more laugh. Don’t wait. 3. Protect your mornings. Stop trading clarity for chaos. The way you start your day sets the tone for everything else. 4. Don’t chase money if it costs your soul. A paycheck without meaning is just another trap. Build a life that feels like yours. 5. Create stories worth telling. At 80, you won’t brag about inbox zero. You’ll brag about the trips, the scars, the risks you took. 6. Do things that scare you. Not skydiving, real fear. Speaking up, walking into a room where you know no one, saying yes when you’re unsure. 7. Treat your body like it’s your greatest asset. Because it is. Eat clean. Move daily. Sleep. Train for freedom, not just aesthetics. 8. Say no more often. Every fake yes chips away at who you are. Protect your peace, even if people don’t understand. 9. Don’t be afraid to pivot. If the old plan doesn’t fit anymore, throw it out. The longer you wait, the harder it gets. 10. Have the hard conversations. The words you don’t say weigh more than the ones you do. Honesty might sting for a moment, but silence lasts forever. 11. Stop coasting. Your 20s feel endless, but they’re not. Every year you drift is momentum you’ll never get back. 12. Don’t confuse busy with fulfilled. I thought 70-hour weeks meant progress. Grinding isn’t always growth. 13. Serve someone who can’t repay you. Volunteer. Mentor. Show up. Giving outside yourself keeps you grounded. 14. Book the trip. Stop waiting for the perfect time. Movement brings life back. 15. Call the people who matter. Text threads and likes aren’t connection. Show up before it’s too late. 16. Make peace with grief. You don’t outrun loss, you learn to carry it differently. Some days it feels lighter, some days it crushes you. Both are normal. 👉Not sure where to even start? DM me ‘STRONG’ and I’ll show you exactly how to build the mindset, habits and body to carry.

t: Most developers immediately say: “Use a Stack
d: Most developers immediately say: “Use a Stack.” And they’re partially correct. But production browsers do a little more than that. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ The Real Problem You accidentally close: → Tab A → Tab B → Tab C Now you click: “Reopen Closed Tab” Chrome restores: Tab C first. Why? Because the most recently closed tab should be restored first. That’s exactly how a Stack works. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Step 1 — Push on Close Every time a tab is closed: Chrome stores: → URL → Title → Session State → Scroll Position onto a stack. Example: Close A Close B Close C Stack: Top → C → B → A ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Step 2 — Pop on Restore When you press: Reopen Closed Tab Chrome removes the top element. Result: C gets restored first. Press again: B gets restored. This follows: LIFO Last In, First Out. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Step 3 — Persist Session Data A simple stack isn’t enough. If Chrome crashes, users still expect recovery. So browsers periodically save tab metadata to disk. Result: ✔ Recovery after restart ✔ Session restoration ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Real Production Design Stack → Stores recently closed tabs Disk Storage → Stores session backup Memory → Provides instant restoration ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Interview Ready Line: “Chrome’s Reopen Closed Tab feature is primarily implemented using a Stack because it follows LIFO behavior. Production browsers enhance this by persisting session metadata to disk for crash recovery and session restoration.” Follow @codedsoul_05 ❤️ #DataStructures #SystemDesign #BackendDevelopment #TechInterview #SoftwareEngineering.

t: A lot of professionals think leadership starts when they get promoted
d: A lot of professionals think leadership starts when they get promoted. It doesn’t. People decide how much authority you have long before your title changes. Some habits quietly reduce your presence at work: 1. Explaining every decision in detail instead of getting to the point 2. Starting sentences with “Sorry” when you’ve done nothing wrong 3. t: One thing consulting completely changed for me was how I give work updates
d: One thing consulting completely changed for me was how I give work updates. Earlier, whenever someone asked for an update, I’d explain everything I’d been working on. The problem was... I was sharing effort instead of clarity. People had to listen to everything before they understood where things actually stood. Then I started using one simple framework. Every update answers four questions: ✅ What’s the current status? ✅ What progress has been made since the last update? ✅ Are there any blockers or risks? ✅ What’s happening next, and by when? That’s it. No long explanations. No unnecessary details. Just the information people actually need to make decisions. The biggest difference wasn’t that my updates became shorter. It was that meetings became quicker, there were fewer follow-up questions, and people trusted that they always knew where things stood. Simple framework. Huge difference. If you want more practical career advice like this, let me know what topic I should cover next..

t: Before you build your next vibe-coded web app, understand this: Getting an app to work is...
d: Before you build your next vibe-coded web app, understand this: Getting an app to work is easy. Building a system that survives real users is the hard part. Most developers focus on features, UI, and deployment. Very few think about what happens after launch. 📊 Database & Scalability • Can your database handle 10,000 users instead of 10? • Are your queries optimized? • Have you added proper indexes? • What happens when your data grows from hundreds to millions of records? A slow database can destroy even the best application. 🔒 Security • Are passwords stored securely? • Are API keys protected? • Is user input validated? • Do you have rate limiting to prevent abuse? • Can bots, scrapers, or attackers exploit your endpoints? If your app is public, someone will eventually test its weaknesses. ⚡ Performance • Are pages loading quickly? • Are APIs optimized? • Are you caching frequently accessed data? • What happens during traffic spikes? Users rarely remember a beautiful UI, but they always remember a slow application. 📈 Monitoring & Logs One of the biggest mistakes developers make is launching without visibility. • Do you have logs? • Error tracking? • Performance monitoring? • Alerts when something breaks? If you can’t see problems, you can’t fix them. 💾 Reliability & Recovery • What happens if your database crashes? • Do you have backups? • Can you recover lost data? • Can you roll back a bad deployment? Every system eventually fails. Great systems recover quickly. 🚀 Reality Check AI can generate code. AI can generate features. AI can generate entire applications. But scalability, security, monitoring, reliability, architecture, and production thinking still require engineering decisions. The question isn’t: “Can I build this?” The better question is: “Can this survive real users, real traffic, real failures, and real-world attacks?” Because building the app is only the beginning. Keeping it running is what separates a demo from a product..

July 20, 1969. A human voice came from the surface of the Moon. The mission had begun four days earlier when the Saturn V rocket lifted Apollo 11 off the Florida coast, shaking the ground with a force no machine had ever produced. The objective was simple to describe and almost impossible to execute: land two men on the Moon and bring them home. By the time the lunar module Eagle separated from the command module, the margin for error was thin. As Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin descended, computer alarms began flashing — 1201 and 1202 program errors. The onboard guidance computer was overloaded. In Houston, engineers had seconds to decide whether to abort. They chose to continue. Fuel was running low. Armstrong looked out the window and realised the automatic landing site was scattered with boulders. He took manual control, flying horizontally across the surface in search of a safer spot. The fuel gauge ticked down — 60 seconds remaining. Then 30. “Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed.” When Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface, the event was broadcast to hundreds of millions of people. The image was grainy, the audio slightly delayed, but the symbolism was clear. A species that had spent its existence confined to one planet was standing on another world. The mission lasted just over eight days. The astronauts collected rock samples, planted a flag, and left behind a plaque that read, “We came in peace for all mankind.” Apollo 11 was not just a technical achievement. Night is when your scalp absorbs oil best. 2 drops of castor oil massaged in before sleep works harder than any hair serum you can buy. 4. Late nights destroy growth hormone production. Growth hormone peaks between 10pm and 2am during deep sleep. That is when your scalp repairs itself. Every hour past midnight you stay awake is an hour of repair your hair does not get. 5. Sleeping with hair tied tightly causes traction alopecia. Constant pulling on the hairline while sleeping permanently weakens those follicles over time. Sleep with hair loose or in a very loose braid. Never tight. Not genetics. Never was. Just habits you did not know were wrong. Save this tonight before you sleep. Which one are you guilty of? t: Let’s be honest, nobody wakes up one day and just quits
d: Let’s be honest, nobody wakes up one day and just quits. The groundwork for a massive career jump happens entirely behind the scenes, often right under the nose of management. If you are planning your next move, here is the ultimate stealth blueprint: 1. The Stealth Mode LinkedIn Update: Before you touch a single word on your profile, go to your settings and turn off “Share profile updates with your network.” Update your skills, optimize your headline for recruiters, and let the algorithm do the work while your current team remains completely oblivious. 2. The “Extended Filter Coffee” Strategy: Suddenly taking 45-minute walks outside or locking yourself in a phone booth? That’s the classic sign of a techie handling recruiter screening calls. ☕ 3. The Calendar Defense: Start blocking “Focus Time” or “Deep Work” blocks on your calendar. It protects your current deliverables so your performance doesn’t drop, while freeing up your mental bandwidth to solve LeetCode problems or review System Design frameworks in peace. 4. The Hidden Networking Loop: Applying directly to job portals is a black hole. The real switches happen through backchannel DMs. Reach out to ex-colleagues or college seniors at your target companies. A warm referral trumps a cold application 100% of the time. 5. The Off-Peak Interviewing Rule: Schedule your technical rounds for early mornings (before standup) or late evenings. If it has to be during the day, use your casual leaves wisely—never stack interviews on a heavy release day. The secret to a successful switch isn’t just being good at interviews; it’s mastering the art of the quiet hustle. 🚀 💬 What’s your ultimate secret tip for managing interview prep alongside a full-time job? Same internet. Same users. Different system design. 🧵 At 10:00 AM sharp,lakhs of users hit “Book Tatkal” at the exact same second. The real problem? 👀 It’s not a weak server. It’s a massive traffic spike:🚨 10 lakh users🚨 One critical second🚨 Millions of concurrent requests Like an entire stadium crowd trying to enter through one tiny gate. So how do scalable systems survive this? 👇 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ✅ Virtual Waiting Room (Message Queue) Never allow all users to hit the database directly. Instead:→ Put booking requests into a queue→ Process requests in controlled order→ Prevent sudden DB overload Result:✔ Stable servers✔ No crash during traffic burst 💡 Like a bank token system:Everyone gets a number and waits their turn. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ✅ Cache Train Data (Redis) Train routes, timings, and seat info don’t change every millisecond. So:→ Store frequently accessed data in Redis→ Avoid querying DB repeatedly→ Reduce database pressure massively Result:⚡ Ultra-fast reads⚡ Lower latency⚡ Better scalability 💡 Like a waiter memorizing the menu instead of running to kitchen every time. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ✅ Load Balancer One server cannot handle lakhs of users alone. So:→ Load balancer distributes traffic across multiple servers→ If one server fails, others continue handling requests Result:✔ High availability✔ Fault tolerance✔ Zero downtime during heavy traffic 💡 Like opening 20 railway counters instead of just one. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ✅ Distributed Seat Locking Imagine two users trying to book:🚂 Seat 32, Coach B2 Without locking:❌ Double booking happens Solution:→ Temporarily lock seat during payment→ Confirm after successful payment→ Release if payment fails/timeouts Result:✔ Consistent booking system✔ No duplicate seat allocation 💡 Similar to an e-commerce cart reservation system. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🧠 Production-Level Concepts Used.

t: 🎯 Interview Question: “If an API works in Postman but fails in the browser, how would you...
d: 🎯 Interview Question: “If an API works in Postman but fails in the browser, how would you troubleshoot it?” ✅ Strong Interview Answer: If an API works in Postman but fails in the browser, my first assumption is that the issue is related to browser-enforced security or request differences, because browsers and Postman behave differently. Here’s how I troubleshoot it step-by-step: 🔹 1. Check Browser DevTools I first open the Browser Developer Tools (F12) → Network tab and inspect: * Request URL * Headers * Response status * Console errors This immediately helps identify whether the issue is from the frontend, browser, or backend. 🔹 2. Check for CORS Issues (Most Common) Browsers enforce CORS policies, while Postman does not. If the backend is not allowing the frontend origin, the browser blocks the request. 🔹 3. Verify Preflight OPTIONS Request Browsers send an OPTIONS request before the actual API call. If the server does not handle OPTIONS correctly, the request fails before reaching the API. 🔹 4. Compare Request Headers I compare the browser request with the Postman request to verify: * Authorization header * Content-Type * Custom headers * Cookies or tokens Sometimes Postman sends headers automatically that the frontend is missing. 🔹 5. Check Authentication & Cookies The browser may not send: * Access token * Session cookie * SameSite cookies This can cause 401 or unauthorized errors. 🔹 6. Verify HTTPS / Mixed Content If the frontend runs on HTTPS and the API runs on HTTP, browsers block the request for security reasons. 🔹 7. Check CSRF & Security Policies Some applications require CSRF tokens for browser requests, which Postman bypasses. 🔹 8. Validate Environment & API URL Sometimes the frontend points to the wrong API environment or incorrect endpoint. ✅ My Debugging Approach: I compare the browser request with the Postman request using the Network tab, identify the exact difference, and then fix the frontend, backend, or API gateway configuration accordingly. 💡 Key Takeaway: Postman bypasses many browser security restrictions, but browsers strictly enforce them — that’s why APIs can behave dif.

t: Shyam Singha Roy ♥️ The story follows Vasudev Ghanta, a young filmmaker in modern-day...
d: Shyam Singha Roy ♥️ The story follows Vasudev Ghanta, a young filmmaker in modern-day Hyderabad who quits his IT job to pursue cinema. To make his debut short film, he casts a psychology student named Keerthi. During the shoot, Vasu experiences strange episodes of temporary memory loss and personality shifts, particularly after getting into a fight where he suffers a head injury. Despite these hitches, his short film becomes a massive hit, leading to a blockbuster feature film. However, at the peak of his success, Vasu is arrested on charges of plagiarism. A publishing house from Kolkata claims that his film’s story is a frame-by-frame copy of works written by a famous Bengali author from the 1970s named Shyam Singha Roy. To prove his innocence and understand why he wrote a story he never actually read, Vasu undergoes clinical hypnosis with the help of Keerthi’s professor. Under hypnosis, he regresses into his past life as Shyam Singha Roy. In the 1970s, Shyam was a fierce, high-caste revolutionary writer in West Bengal who fought against social evils like untouchability and the Devadasi system. During a Navratri festival, he falls in love with Maitreyi, a Devadasi whom he calls Rosie. Shyam challenges the oppressive temple authorities, eventually rescuing Rosie and escaping to Kolkata. There, they build a life together, and Shyam becomes a legendary literary figure, using his pen to advocate for women’s rights and social reform. The tragedy of the past is revealed when it’s shown that Shyam was betrayed and murdered by his own cousins, who coveted his property and despised his radical ideologies. In the present, the court case reaches a climax as legal teams argue over the possibility of reincarnation. Vasu travels to Kolkata to find the remnants of his past life and discovers that an elderly Rosie is still alive, having spent decades waiting for him. #shyamsingharoy #loveedits #lovemusic #edits #fyp.

Follow @ca.mahima_dhing and understand these terms: 👉🏻CTC (Cost to Company) – Total amount the company claims it spends on you Includes salary + bonuses + PF + insurance + gratuity Not what you get in hand 👉🏻Basic / Base Salary – Core fixed salary PF, gratuity, HRA are calculated on this Very important for long‑term growth 👉🏻Fixed Pay – Guaranteed amount paid monthly Includes: Basic + HRA + other fixed allowances Excludes bonuses & incentives 👉🏻Variable Pay/ Performance bonus – Linked to performance or targets May be paid monthly / quarterly / annually Not guaranteed → don’t count it blindly 👉🏻In‑Hand Salary – What actually comes into your bank account = Fixed pay − PF − tax − other deductions This is what matters for monthly expenses 👉🏻PF – Retirement savings (12% of basic) Employer + Employee contribution Reduces in‑hand salary now, helps later 👉🏻Gratuity – Paid after 5 years of continuous service Included in CTC Not paid monthly (many people miss this!) 👉🏻ESOPs/ RSUs – Company shares instead of cash High upside possible Depends on vesting & company performance 🎯 “Never negotiate salary on CTC alone - negotiate on IN‑HAND.” [ CA Mahima Dhing , salary , terms , ctc , in hand , fixed salary , salary ] #fyp.

t: Make your KT (Knowledge Transfer) phase productive—don’t just depend on others, take...
d: Make your KT (Knowledge Transfer) phase productive—don’t just depend on others, take initiative. 1. Ask freely Don’t hesitate to ask questions, even if they feel basic. It’s better to clarify early than stay confused later. When you ask openly, you learn faster and avoid mistakes. 2. Keep it short and focused Instead of long, tiring meetings, request short 10–15 minute sessions on one specific topic. People are more likely to help, and you’ll understand better. 3. Learn while adding value Offer to update or organize existing documents. This helps the team and also gives you a chance to ask relevant questions while working. 4. Record for future use Whenever someone explains something, ask if you can record it. This helps you revisit the steps later and reduces repeated questions. 5. Confirm your understanding Instead of asking “How does this work?”, say “This is what I understood…” and let them correct you. It saves their time and shows your effort. 6. Connect with recent joiners Talk to someone who joined a few months ago. They’ve recently gone through the same phase and can share practical tips and shortcuts. 7. Learn by observing Ask to shadow someone while they work. Watching real tasks helps you understand faster than only listening to explanations. 8. Don’t stay stuck too long If you’re stuck on something, try for 30 minutes. If you still can’t solve it, ask for help. Don’t waste hours just trying to figure it out alone. 9. Communicate your intent Tell your manager what’s slowing you down and that you want to learn faster. This shows ownership and helps you get the right support. t: I’m a dermatologist, and when it comes to hair loss, patients often focus on the wrong...
d: I’m a dermatologist, and when it comes to hair loss, patients often focus on the wrong “miracle” products while ignoring the actual physiology of the scalp. Save this before you spend another rupee on “hair growth” gummies. 🧬👇 * The Scalp Microbiome also Matters like your face Infrequent washing leads to oxidized sebum and Malassezia overgrowth. This triggers micro-inflammation around the follicular unit, which can accelerate shedding in those predisposed to thinning. Cleanse your scalp effectively to protect the follicle. • The “Three-Month Lag” (Telogen Effluvium) If you are seeing excess shedding today, look back at what happened 3 months ago. Whether it was a high fever, extreme stress, or a crash diet, the biological “shock” pushes hair into the Telogen (resting) phase. By the time it falls out, the trigger is usually gone. • Ketoconazole: More Than Just Anti-Dandruff Beyond treating dandruff, 2% Ketoconazole has a mild anti-androgenic effect. It helps disrupt the DHT pathway at the scalp level. For my androgenetic alopecia patients, I often recommend it as a medicated companion to topical minoxidil. • The Ferritin Factor Hair is “non-essential” tissue. Your body prioritizes vital organs first. Even if your iron is “normal,” a low-normal Ferritin (stored iron) can drive chronic shedding. For optimal cycles, we look for levels well above the laboratory minimum. • Dermarolling vs Dermastamping Mechanical stimulation triggers a wound-healing response in the bulge area. However, “rolling” can cause micro-tearing of the hair shaft. I prefer vertical “stamping” or professional microneedling to target depth without unnecessary trauma. The clinical truth: Hair health is a reflection of internal health, hormones, and scalp hygiene. One small mistake and it becomes, “She’s distracted.” 🚫 “Who said what in the other team?” (Gossip) Even if everyone is doing it — don’t. The moment you repeat something, you become part of the rumour mill. And trust quietly drops. Corporate growth isn’t just about skills. It’s about perception. t: In the Indian corporate sector, this isn't about promising a lifetime of servitude
d: In the Indian corporate sector, this isn't about promising a lifetime of servitude. It’s about showing stability, ambition, and cultural fit. Gen Z, Millennials, and Seasoned Pros—everyone answers this differently. Here are 5 distinct answers reflecting different mindsets common in the Indian job market. 1. The Growth-Oriented Professional (The Startup & MNC Hybrid) Scenario: You are in a mid-level role (e.g., Team Lead or Assistant Manager) looking for fast growth but want to show loyalty. Answer: “I see this role as a long-term partnership. I typically look for a horizon of 3 to 5 years to truly make an impact. However, what keeps me at a company is internal growth. If I see a clear path—like moving from a Team Lead to a Project Manager within this timeframe—and I’m learning consistently, I don’t see why I would leave. I’m looking for a place where I can build a legacy, not just serve a notice period.” 2. The Project-Oriented Realist (The IT Services & Consultant) Scenario: Working in a service-based firm (like TCS, Infosys, or a Big 4) where projects have defined cycles. Answer: “Honestly, I am looking for stability to see through a full project lifecycle. I’d ideally want to commit at least 4 years to this organization. Coming from the service industry, I know that the first year is about absorbing the domain knowledge, the next two are about delivering results, and the fourth is about mentoring juniors. I want to avoid the 'job-hopping' tag and truly master this domain with your organization.” 3. The Stability Seeker (The Legacy Indian Corporate) 4. The High-Performance Ambitious (The MBA / Tier-1 Grad) 5. The Skills-Focused Gen Z (The New Age Digital Native) 📌 Comment “Answer” to get the remaining 3 answers—I’ll send them to you in your DM. ✨ Remember: In India, HR doesn't want to hear 'till retirement' (it sounds fake) or '1 year' (it sounds risky). “WhatsApp has billions of users. So where are all the messages stored?” Mostly… not on their servers. WhatsApp uses End-to-End Encryption (E2EE). When you send a message: - It’s encrypted on your device - Routed through WhatsApp’s servers - Delivered to the recipient - Removed from server memory after delivery The server acts as a relay, not a long-term archive. That’s why: - If you switch phones without a cloud backup, chats are gone - WhatsApp cannot “restore” conversations they never stored Backups (if enabled) live in services like iCloud or Google Drive — encrypted separately. Architecturally, this design does two powerful things: - Maximizes privacy - Minimizes centralized storage burden At global scale, storing every message permanently would require enormous long-term storage infrastructure. Instead, persistence happens primarily at the edge — on user devices. This is not just a privacy feature. It’s an architectural decision. At scale, the smartest system is often the one that stores less. t: 1️⃣ Everything Is Always “Urgent” Every task is marked urgent
d: 1️⃣ Everything Is Always “Urgent” Every task is marked urgent. Every deadline is unrealistic. When everything is urgent, nothing is actually planned. 2️⃣ People Are Afraid to Speak Honestly Meetings feel quiet. People agree publicly… then complain privately. That’s a culture of fear. 3️⃣ Good Employees Keep Leaving High performers don’t stay long. When the best people keep leaving, it’s rarely a coincidence. 4️⃣ Feedback Only Comes When Something Is Wrong No recognition. No appreciation. Only criticism when something fails. That environment drains motivation. 5️⃣ Work-Life Balance Is Treated Like Laziness Leaving on time is questioned. Taking breaks is judged. Healthy companies respect boundaries. 6️⃣ No One Explains the “Why” You’re told what to do. But never why it matters. That usually means leadership lacks clarity. 7️⃣ Mistakes Are Punished, Not Learned From People hide errors instead of fixing them. Because mistakes lead to blame, not improvement. That kills innovation. 8️⃣ Promotions Feel Random The hardest workers aren’t progressing. Instead, visibility and favoritism decide growth. That breaks trust. 9️⃣ Communication Is Always Chaotic Last-minute decisions. Constant confusion. People finding out information too late. Chaos is not a strategy. 🔟 Everyone Looks Tired All the Time Not just busy. Mentally drained. Energy in the office feels heavy. That’s usually a sign of deeper problems. A good company doesn’t feel perfect. But it feels fair. If several of these signs sound familiar, it might be time to reassess your environment. Save this for the day you start questioning your workplace. #corporatelife #careeradvice #workplaceculture #professionaldevelopment #earlycareer worklifebalancetips.

t: At 22, your job isn’t to shine
d: At 22, your job isn’t to shine. It’s to become difficult to replace. Here are things I wish i knew when i was 22 1️⃣ Pick roles that teach you how decisions are made, not just how tasks are done. At 22, avoid jobs where you only execute. You should be sitting in meetings, reading notes, watching how seniors decide, argue, and compromise. What to do: choose roles where you’re close to managers, clients, officers, or leadership, even if the title sounds small. 2️⃣ Start building proof of work from day one Your memory won’t save you. Your manager won’t remember everything. Proof will. What to do: maintain one simple folder with reports, decks, mails, outcomes, numbers. This becomes your leverage for switches, interviews, and raises. 3️⃣ Learn one hard skill that makes you useful everywhere Not vibes. Not “communication”. One real skill: writing clearly, Excel, research, data analysis, policy drafting, financial modeling. What to do: pick one and go deep for 6-12 months until people start coming to you for it. This isn’t motivation. This is damage control for your future. Your 20s don’t ruin careers loudly. They do it slowly, through comfort, confusion, and delay. Save this. Read it twice. Act early. d: This is a classic system design interview question — and it’s NOT about servers or databases 🤯 | The problem isn’t compute. | It’s distance 🌍 | When a user in India opens your website | and your servers are in the US, | every request travels thousands of kilometers ✈️ | Images 🖼️ | CSS 🎨 | JavaScript ⚙️ | All crossing oceans 🌊 | More distance = more latency ⏳ | Adding more backend servers in the US ❌ | Optimizing code ❌ | Neither fixes this problem. | The correct answer is: use a CDN ✅ | A CDN (Content Delivery Network) caches static content | like images, videos, CSS, and JavaScript | on servers distributed across the world 🌐 | So instead of an Indian user fetching content from the US, | they get it from a nearby edge location ⚡ | Same website. | Same backend. | 🚀 Much lower latency. | That’s why CDNs are one of the first answers interviewers expect | when performance varies by geography. | #hld #softwaredevelopment #softwarejobs #systemdesign #cdn

t: Day 305/365: This is Nihar, your usual 9 to 5 corporate guy working as a Tech consultant...
d: Day 305/365: This is Nihar, your usual 9 to 5 corporate guy working as a Tech consultant in SF. I made the mistake of saying Yes to my first job offer without asking a single question. Later, I found out others at the same level were earning more. Here is what I learned to do before accepting an offer. 1. Always ask for time Say: Thank you for the offer, can get 24 hours to review it? 2. Check total compensation Go beyond CTC. Look at fixed pay, bonus, PF, insurance, and allowances. 3.Use market benchmarks Based on my research, similar roles are in the range of X-Y. Can we align closer to that? This shows you know your value without sounding aggressive. 4.Negotiate benefits if salary is fixed. Extra leave, joining bonus, relocation support, training budget. These add real value. 5. Put it in writing Confirm everything by email. Handshakes and calls fade, written proof doesn't. This one step can change how much you earn and how secure you feel in your new role. . . . . . . . . 🔐 Keywords 9to5 life, office, software engineering, corporate life, corporate, pune, salesforce, engineering, switch, career, mindset, weekdays, weekends, office life, 9 to 5, Job switch, HR 📌 Hashtags #gym #fitness #viral #corporate #9to5 #9to5life #office #officememe #corporatememes #funny #funvideos #fun#trendingreel #fyp #viralvideos #trend #relatable #switch #softwareengineering #engineering #career #life#jobs.

Location 👇 | . | 📍Thirumalai Nayakar Palace, Madurai 🏰✨ | Built in the 17th century by King Tirumala Nayak, this majestic palace in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, is one of the city’s must-visit landmarks. Once considered among the wonders of South India, the Thirumalai Nayakar Palace still stands as a stunning example of grandeur and royal vision. | While Madurai is world-famous for the Meenakshi Amman Temple, there’s a lot more to explore — and this palace definitely deserves a spot on your list. | Originally constructed in 1636, the palace was about four times larger than what remains today. King Tirumala Nayak wanted to build a masterpiece fit for royalty, and it’s believed that he even brought in an Italian architect to help design it. The result is an incredible mix of Dravidian, Islamic, and European architectural styles. | In the 18th century, the king’s grandson partially demolished the structure to build his own palace in Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) — a project that was never completed. Later, Lord Napier, a British administrator, restored parts of the original palace, which then served as a British administrative office. | ✨ What to See Inside | Courtyard & Main Hall: | Step through the entrance and you’ll reach the courtyard leading to the grand main hall. This was once the king’s residence, known for its intricate stucco designs and beautifully carved arches. | Dance Hall (Nataka Shala): | This was where the king enjoyed traditional dance performances accompanied by live music and torchlight. There was once a temple and garden beside it, dedicated to Goddess Rajarajeswari — both now lost to time. | Light & Sound Show: | Every evening, the palace hosts a light and sound show — 6:45 PM (English) and 8:00 PM (Tamil) — that runs for about 45 minutes. t: what really sets you apart—especially in interviews—are these 10 must-have skills (save...
d: what really sets you apart—especially in interviews—are these 10 must-have skills (save this!): Here’s what I wish I knew earlier—the 10 skills every dev should start with 1. Master your language basics Don’t just copy code—learn why things work. Challenge yourself with small projects. 2. Data structures & algorithms This is problem-solving 101. Start simple: learn arrays, stacks, and sorting. Practice with daily coding puzzles. 3. Git is gold Create a GitHub repo, play with branches, and commit often. You’ll avoid “I lost my code!” panic forever. 4. Debugging & testing Hit errors? That’s normal! Trace bugs with print/logs, set breakpoints, write simple tests to check your code before you launch. 5. Linux basics change everything Commands like `ls`, `cd`, `rm`, and `grep` mean you don’t have to fear the terminal. Explore files, automate chores, and feel like a real hacker. 6. APIs & JSON Make your app talk to others—fetch weather, send emails, whatever! Use Postman to experiment and learn to read JSON like a storybook. 7. Learn cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) Try a free tier. Deploy a sample app. See your code run online—it’s the future, and most jobs want this. 8. Docker & DevOps basics Build a Dockerfile, run your app in a container. Learn what CI/CD is (auto-testing/deploying). Suddenly your code works everywhere, not just your laptop. 9. Databases: SQL & NoSQL Understand how to store, query, and update data. Practice simple CRUD with SQLite or MongoDB—every app needs to remember stuff! 10.	Communicate like a pro Write clear comments, document your work, and talk with your team. Great projects need teamwork! Drop a “💡” if this helped! Read here! | You wake up, look in the mirror, and your face feels puffy. First thought? “Maybe I didn’t sleep well or maybe I should just wash my face with cold water and it’ll go away.” But the truth is that’s not how face bloating works. Cold water might help a little, but it won’t fix the actual problem. | The real reason your face looks bloated is usually because of too much salt, dehydration, poor sleep, or late-night eating. d: Here is the list⬇️ (Before you read this, kindly note that the intention here was not to promote bias or unfair practices. It was simply to highlight a common mistake that often leads to resumes being rejected, so jobseekers can avoid it. The job market is tough, and our goal is to help you stay ahead and make your application stronger) 1/ Fancy canva made resume When I see a canva made colorful resume, I know the candidate wanted an easy shortcut. A resume is not an art project. It’s a document that should be clear, direct, and easy to read. 2/ Soft skills with no proof As a recruiter, I do not get impressed by skills like “Team player”, “Hard worker”. ......... These words mean nothing without proof. What I want to see instead: • Real achievements • Specific projects • Challenges you overcame • Impact you made 3/ Listing every job you ever did Even the ones that have nothing to do with the role. It wastes my time and yours. 4/ Long, Chunky Paragraphs No recruiter have time to dive deep into your resume. We get 100s of them. Add bullet, be crisp and clear with your information. 5/ Objective statement. As a recruiter, I know why have you applied. Instead I would want to see a simple 3-4 lines summary {resume, resume tips, resume guide, resume guidelines, perfect resume, best resume, ats resume, ats friendly resume, resume tips for you, what to include in a resume, what not to include in a resume, career, career growth, jobs, get job faster} #resume #resumé #resumehelp #resumetips #resumebuilding #resumeservices #cvtips #atsresume #career.

t: Stop giving textbook answers in interviews Most students stop at lines like: “Database is...
d: Stop giving textbook answers in interviews Most students stop at lines like: “Database is a collection of data” or “DBMS is software used to manage data.” But if you want to truly stand out, you need to go beyond memorized definitions. Here’s the trick: A Database is simply a collection of organized data, think student records, vendor lists, or customer info. But the DBMS? That’s the God of Data, a powerful tool that doesn’t just store information. It creates, manages, updates, and even deletes data efficiently using systems like MySQL, Oracle, or SQL Server. The difference is subtle, but crucial. When you explain it with context or a real-world example, the interviewer doesn’t just hear your answer, they remember your thought process. Next time you face a technical or HR question, don’t just recite facts. Add a little spark, make them smile, and show your understanding. That’s the secret to leaving a lasting impression! t: How I learn multiple languages at the same time, without EVER mixing them up
d: How I learn multiple languages at the same time, without EVER mixing them up...⁠ ⁠ YES, it’s possible.⁠ No, you don’t need to be a genius.⁠ But there are things to keep in mind!⁠ Here’s what works (and what will save your sanity):⁠ ⁠ ⁠ 1. Don’t start two new languages at once.⁠ This is rule #1.⁠ If your newest language isn’t at least B1 (low-intermediate), don’t add another one yet.⁠ ⁠ 2. Choose languages that are very different. (at the start)⁠ Spanish & Italian? Norwegian & Swedish? Be so real with yourself, you're bound to mix those up.⁠ Instead, go for contrast:⁠ ⁠ French + Japanese⁠ German + Korean⁠ Arabic + Portuguese⁠ ⁠ (After you've really nailed down a language, you can totally learn another one that's similar.)⁠ ⁠ 3. Assign each language a different intensity.⁠ Here’s what I do:⁠ ⁠ 🌱 Maintenance mode – Just 15 min a day (immersion)⁠ ☘️ Gradual improvement – 30 min a day (casual focused study)⁠ 🌳 Turbo focus – 1–2 hours daily, deeper work⁠ ⁠ This keeps your energy focused while making gradual gains across all your langs.⁠ ⁠ ⁠ 4. Consume different types of content in each one.⁠ This usually happens naturally because every culture shines in different genres:⁠ ⁠ Japanese = anime/game shows⁠ Spanish = soap operas⁠ Korean = k-dramas/reality tv⁠ French = cinema⁠ ⁠ Associate each language with a specific genre or vibe.⁠ It creates strong mental links and helps distinguish the languages even more in your brain.⁠ ⁠ Which languages are you learning right now? Do you find them easy to juggle? ⁠ ⁠ #learnfrench #learnspanish #polyglot #languagelearning #multilingual #bilingual.

t: Cleaning silver with hot water, baking soda, salt, and aluminum foil uses a simple...
d: Cleaning silver with hot water, baking soda, salt, and aluminum foil uses a simple electrolysis reaction. When silver items are placed in a container lined with aluminum foil and covered with the mixture, a chemical reaction begins. The baking soda and salt help transfer electrons between the tarnished silver and the aluminum. Through this process, the sulfur that caused the tarnish (silver sulfide) is pulled away from the silver and bonds with the aluminum instead, leaving the silver clean and shiny without scrubbing or harsh chemicals. #SilverCleaningHack #ElectrolysisCleaning #DIYCleaning #EcoFriendlyClean #BakingSodaMagic #RestoreSilver #HomeScience #explore #fyp #instareel.

t: Japan converts footsteps into electricity using piezoelectric tiles
d: Japan converts footsteps into electricity using piezoelectric tiles. These tiles capture the kinetic energy from your steps. When you walk, your weight and motion create pressure on the tiles. The tiles bend slightly, producing mechanical stress. Piezoelectric materials inside the tiles convert this stress into electrical energy. Each step generates a small charge, and millions of steps together produce enough power to run LED lights, digital displays, and sensors. In busy places like Shibuya Station, around 2.4 million footsteps a day contribute to this system. The electricity is stored or used immediately, reducing reliance on traditional power sources and supporting sustainable urban infrastructure. This method turns everyday motion into practical renewable energy. #japan #knowledge #facts #didyouknow #fyp #technology #innovation #history #tech #experiments #viral

1. He didn’t drink. He didn’t smoke. But he slept after midnight 300+ nights in a row. That wasn’t “grind” — it was a vascular tax he never paid. 2. Past-midnight sleep acts like jet lag on repeat. Your circadian clock mis-times hormones; blood pressure stays high at night when it should fall (nocturnal “dip”). 3. No dip = quiet damage. Vessels stiffen, plaques inflame, clots form easier. The risk stacks with every month of short, late sleep. 4. Brain signs you ignore: morning headaches, jaw clench, brain fog, vertigo on standing, memory that works by noon. 5. Heart signs you excuse: resting pulse 5–10 bpm higher than last year, winded on stairs, chest “buzz” after coffee, skipped beats in bed. 6. Sleep debt also spikes blood sugar and inflammation; add stress, high salt takeout, weekend booze, and “healthy” labs hide a pressure cooker. 7. The trap: you feel fine at 30–35 — then a clot meets a narrowed artery on a random Tuesday. Not fate; arithmetic. 8. If your watch says 5–6h and you “function,” that’s coping, not health. The brain clears plaques in deep sleep; the heart resets during a real nocturnal dip. 9. What would have saved him (screenshot this): • Lights out by 11 pm 5+ nights/week; dim screens 60–90 min before. • Check home BP morning & evening for 7 days; log the numbers. • Aim <120/80 average; if ≥130/80 repeatedly — see a clinician. • Loud snoring or stop–start breathing? Get screened for sleep apnea. • Cut late caffeine; last dose before 2 pm. • Salt audit: restaurant food carries the day’s sodium in one sitting. • Move 20–30 min daily; walk after dinner. • Keep weight in check; neck size and reflux fuel apneas. 10. ER cheat sheet (don’t be a hero): FAST — Face droop, Arm weakness, Speech trouble, Time to call emergency. One hour = months of recovery. 11. If you’re 25–40, ask your doctor for BP, lipids, A1C now, not “someday.” Quiet numbers today prevent loud nights later. 12. Not fear — math. Late, short sleep robs the brain of its repair window and the heart of its nightly pressure drop. Correct the clock, and risk drops too. Follow @tim_torshel for more — and save this..

t: Here’s a roadmap to help you go from a software engineer to a data scientist 👩‍💻 👇 If...
d: Here’s a roadmap to help you go from a software engineer to a data scientist 👩‍💻 👇 If you’re tired of writing vanilla apps and want to build ML systems instead, this one’s for you. Step 1 – Learn Python and SQL (not Java, C++, or JavaScript). → Focus on pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, matplotlib → For SQL: use LeetCode or StrataScratch to practice real-world queries → Don’t just write code—learn to think in data Step 2 – Build your foundation in statistics + math. → Start with Practical Statistics for Data Scientists → Learn: probability, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, distributions → Brush up on linear algebra (vectors, dot products) and calculus (gradients, chain rule) Step 3 – Learn ML the right way. → Do Andrew Ng’s ML course (Deeplearning.ai) → Master the full pipeline: cleaning → feature engineering → modeling → evaluation → Read Elements of Statistical Learning or Sutton & Barto if you want to go deeper Step 4 – Build 2–3 real, messy projects. → Don’t follow toy tutorials → Use APIs or scrape data, build full pipelines, and deploy using Streamlit or Gradio → Upload everything to GitHub with a clear README Step 5 – Become a storyteller with data. → Read Storytelling with Data by Cole Knaflic → Learn to explain your findings to non-technical teams → Practice communicating precision/recall/F1 in simple language Step 6 – Stay current. Never stop learning. → Follow PapersWithCode (it's now sun-setted, use huggingface.co/papers/trending, ArXiv Sanity, and follow ML practitioners on LinkedIn → Join communities, follow researchers, and keep shipping new experiments ------- Save this for later. Tag a friend who’s trying to make the switch. t: I get a lot of DMs asking me how I got my forearms to look like this
d: I get a lot of DMs asking me how I got my forearms to look like this. One thing that I do is - getting chalk on my hands and grabbing the thickest plates in the gym, holding them up for about 30 seconds. Repeat this for 3 or 4 sets. A fun variation I like to try is - laying the plates flat on the ground and keeping your fingers on the sides and getting them off the ground. Keep adding plates to the stack and keep the weights off the ground for as long as you can. Your forearms are always trained passively in the gym. I like to intentionally train them by alternating my hands to rack and re-rack weights. Train to increase grip strength and your forearms will get bigger. Trust me, the ladies will love it - they're both aesthetic and very functional ;) Increasing grip strength allows you to do fun stuff that I liked to call circus time. #fitness #gripstrength #calisthenics #powerlifting #menswellness #mensfashion #forearm #.
